items.s: Four Champions at Sport City Report and results of Belgrave athletes at the AAA Championships at Sport City, Manchester, with titles for Goldie Sayers, Tim Benjamin, Tim Bayley and Ben Challenger. AAA Championships Sport City, Manchester, 9-10 July 2005. a=9, b=10 Four Champions at Sport City There was some dispute as to whether the ex-Commonwealth Games warm up track was really suitable for the AAA Championships. Certainly the stadium cannot take anything like the crowds that used to attend such events. But there was plenty of claret & gold in evidence and with four champions and nine other medallists it was a good championships for Belgrave and for our sponsors adidas. A third successive javelin title went to Goldie Sayers who although a little down on distance in this competition has thrown a lifetime best of 61.45 metres this summer. Goldie is confident that she’s in shape to get to the World Championship final and maybe reach out to 63 metres. Tim Benjamin was the favourite in the 400 metres in spite of missing much pre-season conditioning, suffering a cold in the run up to the event and facing up to a Woodford Green onslaught in the form of Davis and Hedman. He came through it all with flying colours although he admitted to having to work really hard in the home straight. With Windsor’s James McIlroy in the field it was unlikely that anyone was tipping Tim Bayley as the 800 metres winner – but win he did – grabbing the lead while McIlroy faded, ultimately to drop out, and holding on grimly all the way to the finish. Now, if he can just get the qualifying time, surely Tim’s earned a trip to the Commonwealth Games in Melbourne. A season’s best saw Ben Challenger in complete control of the high jump and in Helsinki a height of 2.30m, equal to his lifetime best achieved six years ago, is not out of the question. items.h: Rugby put the boot in – no Cup final for Belgrave in 2005!
items.sum: Report and results of the Golden Jubilee Cup semi-final at Derby Moorways, where Belgrave finished second to Rugby & Northants by two points and missed the final.
items.s: Rugby put the boot in – no Cup final for Belgrave in 2005! Report and results of the Golden Jubilee Cup semi-final at Derby Moorways, where Belgrave finished second to Rugby & Northants by two points and missed the final. Golden Jubilee Cup Semi-Final, Derby Moorways, 16 July 2005. Rugby put the boot in – no Cup final for Belgrave in 2005! “Are you sure there’s no-one else who could do the 400 relay?” Kevin Sempers implored of the Team Manager. “Well there is just one guy,” replied the bearded one, “but he's out there with two more laps to go in the steeplechase at the moment!” Kevin turned to see forty-two year-old Paul Beaumont plodding down the straight on his way to earning 7 points for a second place. “Ok,” said Kevin with a smile, “I'm knackered - but I'll do it.” Multi-event star Kevin had pulled out of the team two days earlier, suffering from an adductor strain, but the night before the match he’phoned up to say that maybe it wasn’t quite so bad, and perhaps he’d come along to see how things went. He ended up doing six events, taking in four wins - and all this with an important decathlon lined up in two weeks time. Kevin wasn’t the only hero. We’ve already mentioned veteran 400 hurdler Paul Beaumont turning out for the ’chase. Jonathan Blackledge injured himself while winning the 800m and had to pull out of the 1500 - but then David Anderson, with his Achilles tendon already sore from the 5k, stepped into the breach saying he’d jog round; of course he then couldn’t resist having a pop at the field on the last lap. As David limped off to catch his train home we could only hope he hadn’t done himself any long term damage. It was like that all afternoon: Scot Thompson also has an injury problem and would only do the discus - until he saw how a few more points might save the day and offered a “standing” shot put as well; an unfit Darren Chin won the 100m, ran the sprint relay - and then let himself be persuaded to run the long relay; Graham Beasley has been troubled with a trapped nerve but won the 200 and ran both relays; Chrissie Foster placed second in the 800m and then lined up for the very next event, the 100m, to avoid a blank on the team sheet. The long relay boys were promised that we’d pull them out of the 4x400m if it was impossible to win the match but with a flurry of late wins including the women’s long relay, where we were boosted by the arrival of Hannah Stares and Jennifer Culley who’d hot-footed it from Loughborough, we could see that if our men won and Rugby placed fourth – we’d win the match. And then, as they lined up, we found that there were only three teams on the track. It was all over barring dropped batons. We did win the relay – but missed out on a place in the final by a whisker – two points. There were plenty of nightmare events where points could have been gained. We had no runner in the women’s high hurdles and with only one competitor in the race we could have turned out someone to bunny-hop over the barriers to gain 7 points. We also suffered from a pole vault problem – no competitor in the women’s competition and Cameron Johnston coming in late and failing to clear a height in the men’s event. The match at Loughborough (all credit to those who did that and the Cup), the BMC meet at Cardiff, a Heptathlon in Spain and the European U23 Champs. drew heavily on our teams, but whereas the men’s squad have the depth to cope with these demands, the women’s team don’t. Nevertheless, there were bright spots in the women’s team as well. Eva Massey blew the opposition away in the shot and Michelle Nestor, with long and high jump action already behind her, took the triple jump in a near best of 11.47m. It was great to see our men’s winner Farel Mepandy giving Michelle some advice which paid immediate dividends and also to hear respected coach John Anderson tell us what great potential she has. Jacqui Loney was close to her best in the hammer and Louise Cooper came off the roads to gain second in the 3000m. So, that’s it for the Cup in 2005. All credit to everyone on the day who did all they could, but now we can go on holiday in late August! items.h: Win streak comes to an end
items.sum: Bill Laws's report on British Athletics League Match 4 at New River Stadium, Haringey, where Belgrave lost to Woodford Green with Essex Ladies, with the final Division One table.
items.s: Win streak comes to an end Bill Laws's report on British Athletics League Match 4 at New River Stadium, Haringey, where Belgrave lost to Woodford Green with Essex Ladies, with the final Division One table. British Athletics League Match 4, New River Stadium, Haringey, 30 July 2005 Win streak comes to an end Bill Laws writes:- Although there was still a statistical chance that we could retain our League title the real objective as we entered this match was to end the season with a win. And with a number of season bests and pb’s we almost made it, losing out to a victorious Woodford Green with Essex Ladies team. Damage limitation achieved The start was not promising. Only Mick Jones lined up for the hammer and once again finished second best to Andy Frost of WGEL. Points were also down in the pole vault after Cameron Johnson had withdrawn the night before due to injury. Damage limitation was achieved as William Sharman cleared 4 metres for a season’s best and junior Roy Collier equalled his best to get better than expected B points. The long jump saw a welcome return to the fold of Richard Danso - he quit the sport four years ago - who proved that his return was no flash in the pan as he recorded his first ever legal plus 7 metres jump to support a somewhat jaded Adrian Phillips who was recovering from his 30th birthday party celebrations. As Adrian’s head cleared so his jumps improved and two second spots were to mark the change in our fortunes. Next up was Scot Thompson who opened the discus comp with a near 53 metre effort. A distance he was not to improve on and one which Inter-Counties champion Leith Marar chased but could not match; but third and first spots added valuable points. Matt Douglas back in form - Ben Challenger supports the team It was great to see Ben Challenger pair up with William Sharman in the high jump. Ben had delayed his departure to the World Champs warm up camp to support the Belgrave team and pronounced himself satisfied as he had withdrawn from the previous week’s competition at Crystal Palace nursing a slight injury. But here he was, winning, and in the process having some good attempts at 2.30m. William gained a good second place in the B event so the points continued mounting. But we weren’t getting away from WGEL who once again called out the evergreen Dalton Grant. Dalton turns 40 next year and can still clear 2.10m with apparent ease. Matt Douglas has finally overcome a niggling injury and arrived pronouncing that he would fill in any event to gain points. Silly boy! His win in the A 400H was a comfortable affair after he had gone out easy and ran the home straight in style. But an hour and a half later he was called up for the A 110H as William Sharman felt hamstring pain during his warm up strides. Matt hasn’t run the event for two years and not trained over the high hurdles. His pb of 14.10 looked in danger until he hit the last hurdle but third spot in 14.17 was way above anybody’s expectations. Matt later put in a 48.3 relay leg to confirm that his troubles are over, but too late to make a bid for World Championship selection. By coincidence Dominic Girdler ran the same time as Matt to get second in the B race. The 800m didn’t go to plan and Graeme Oudney could not explain why he was 7 seconds down on his season’s best as he trailed in last in the A race. With a paucity of middle distance men doing the League this year Chris Axe was a last minute replacement for the B race, arriving 5 minutes before the start and running within a second of his pb. He later ran his first ever steeplechase to make sure that Will Cockerell had a partner - and it was a surprise to all to seem him outkick Will who had, it must be said, just run the 5000m. For someone who has never jumped a barrier let alone a water jump Chris acquitted himself well. More to come? Sprinters shine Next to the 100m, followed by the 400m. Originally it had been planned to put Graham Beasley and Darren Chin on the starting line. But Graham wasn’t feeling too good and the arrival of World Youth double gold medallist Harry Aikines-Ayreetey for the guest 100m and relay prompted Graham to suggest a change to the line up. Harry duly obliged with a second place and in the B race Darren, running from lane one, also gained a valuable second place in exactly the same time as Harry. But whereas Harry’s race was just over the legal limit, Darren’s wasn’t. So a season’s best for Darren and a quick promotion to the B 200 as Graham suggested James Ellington take the A 200m. James duly obliged with his fastest ever run to gain second place and dip under 21 secs for the first time. Darren followed this with a big season’s best so the last minute changes proved a huge success. Set Osho, back from the European under 20 championships with a long relay gold medal, proved to all and sundry that his long awaited breakthrough has arrived as he set a new pb of 47.35sec which he followed later in the long relay with another sub 48sec clocking. In the B race junior Gavin Selway made his now trademark rocket start and headed the field at 200m only to be caught on the line but it was another great effort from this durable young man who still gained third spot. Darren Gauson, fresh from a 3min 45sec pb in Belgium, joined Stephen Sharp in a tactical but classy 1500m. With third place in the A for Stephen and second in the B for Darren more good points as we briefly hit the front for the first time. A terrible triple jump then moved us back down the placings only for an excellent near max points in the shot for Chris Gearing and Scot Thompson to move us back up again. A high quality javelin competition meant less points than expected although Wesley Smith threw a lifetime’s best and James Everard competed even though he is due for a knee operation on Monday. His spirit exemplified the team’s efforts as at last we seemed to be firing on all cylinders. Exciting relays Finally to the relays. Graham Beasley ran his usual second sector, despite not being well, as the team struggled with another lane 1 draw. Darren Chin’s blocks slipped to add to the tension but then he, Graham, James and Harry clocked the fastest club time in the UK this year and finished some 0.65 seconds ahead of second placers WGEL. The 400m relay was even more exciting. Matt Douglas led the first stage passing to Graham Oudney who fought hard and passed the baton to Set in third spot. Set cruised and then kicked hard to give Gavin Selway a two metre lead ahead of a chasing pack which ominously included Chris Rawlinson for Trafford and Ewan Thomas for the Beagles. Gavin held them until 30 metres from the line, finishing in third spot to record a season’s best for the club. A photo of that finishing straight shoot out would have a memorable place in Gavin’s album. Any shots out there? And yet, after all these heroics, WGEL prevailed. Gladys Bird and her merry men were rightly ecstatic. They have come close to taking the BAL title on several occasions and finally they have achieved their ambition. items.s: Division Four Champions Report, results and final table for UK Women's Athletics League Division 4 Match 3 at Abingdon, where the Belgrave Belles won the division unbeaten. UK Women’s Athletics League Division 4 Match 3, Abingdon, 31 July 2005. Division Four Champions It was fitting that the last match of the year took place at the same stadium that twelve months earlier had seen us miss promotion by just 2 match points. This time everything came right and it would have taken an almighty disaster for the Belles to have missed out again. But it wasn’t just promotion that we were looking for – an unbeaten 2005 campaign would be nice. Blackheath & Bromley weren’t going to make it easy for us and when the opening event – the pole vault – saw two B&B stars and no other competitors, it was tantamount to giving them an 18 point head start. Hannah Stares started the recovery by winning the 400 hurdles and then Claire Robinson took the 800m. As the jumps and throws results then started coming in, we crept slowly towards the lead. Double wins came from Sarah Wellstead and Katryna Euridge in the long jump, a double again in the “triple” with Sarah again and Michelle Nestor close behind her, and it was almost a maximum score in the high jump as well thanks to Hannah and Michelle. With Julie Hollman in the line-up, no-one was going to get near our sprint hurdle duo, and as Julie then turned her attention to the shot where she partnered Eva Massey, it was top points again. It remained for Laura Fox and Jacquie Loney to do the business in the discus and we were away and clear. Congratulations to all who made the league campaign a success - every point scorer - every judge and timekeeper - and especially Team Managers Cynthia and Bob who kept the momentum going. It'll be tougher next year in division three, but there's no reason why we cannot do it again in 2006. 100m: 4 J Culley 12.73/0.8; 2 K Euridge 12.87/1.5. 200m: 2 J Culley 25.59/-0.8; 2 R Lewis 26.81/0.6. 400m: 4 R Lewis 60.06; 4 L Collier 64.35. 800m: 1 C Robinson 2:12.35; 3 S Gailey 2:18.90. 1500m: 6 R Powell 5:00.41; 4 V Goodwin 5:29.15. 3000m: 7 L Cooper 11:26.46; 1 A England 11:32.26. 100mH: 1 J Hollman 14.23/-0.5; 1 H Stares 14.87/1.0. 400mH: 1 H Stares 63.27; 2 V Goodwin 74.22. items.s: National Junior Athletics League Review of the National Junior Athletics League season, with the under-20 women winning the Brent Division, and results from the women's match at Banbury and men's match at Sutton. National Junior Athletics League You’ve got to hand it to our women’s under 20 team who although only small in number had a terrific season to top the Brent Division of the National Junior League – well done to Team Manager Kim Collier. In 2004 our Junior men also won the Brent Division and as a result earned promotion to the Southern Premier Division. But the gulf in standard between the two divisions is huge and although we have some truly outstanding male juniors the rival attractions of World Youth Games and European U20 Championships meant that they mostly gave the NJAL a miss in 2005. As a result we were unable to do ourselves justice. Organisation of the League changes next season when the competition becomes mixed. To form the new league structure the men’s and women’s points for 2005 have been added together and on the club rankings so calculated, Belgrave’s joint men’s and women’s team for 2006 will be placed in the Brent Division. items.s: It’s Wicks in the wet Report of the Julie Button 10 km at Elmbridge, where Phil Wicks beat course record holder Kassa Tadesse and Belgrave moved up to share top spot in the Surrey Road League. Julie Button 10 km, Elmbridge, 24 July 2005. With only two races to go in the Surrey Road League we had some work to do to get on a par with South London Harriers but in spite of the steady drizzle the omens looked good as our course record holder Kassa Tadesse was on hand to defend his title. It was a hard race for Kassa last year, when he had to hold off club-mate Mark Thompson, and this year, too, his toughest opposition came from men wearing claret and gold strip. Phil Wicks made the early pace but as they raced towards Hampton Court, Kassa took up the challenge in the third kilometre and then Erwin McRae led throughout the fourth. The Belgrave trio were now clear but as they reached the halfway mark in 15:38 and turned for home, it was Phil increasing the pressure. Erwin fell away at 6 km as they raced onto the towpath along the Thames – and then Kassa also could hold on to his young challenger no longer. Phil had a comfortable winning margin of 18 seconds by the finish and in spite of the rain and the loose surface over the last few kilometres was within half a minute of his best ever time of 30:29 – a mark that may well be improved when he races for the SEAA in the forthcoming Cardiff 10 km. John Charles equalled his best ever time to become Belgrave’s fourth scorer in the open race, and with the perfect score in the three to count road league we moved up to share top spot in the league table Men. 1 P Wicks (Belgrave) 30:54; 2 K Tadesse 31:12; 3 E McRae 31:14; 8 J Charles 33:07; 14 J Clarke 33:41; 16 L Greatorex 34:08; 43 G Reid M40 36:45; 133 P Cross M50 40:22; 538 finished. items.s: Local heroes Report of Belgrave winning the Nonsuch 4 x 2.2 miles relay for a ninth consecutive time, with Richard Ward called up at the last minute and Phil Wicks taking the lead on the final leg. Road Running Nonsuch 4 x 2.2 miles Relay, Nonsuch Park, 7 July 2005. It was a slightly subdued group of runners, gathering in the Cheam corner of Nonsuch Park after the day’s terrorist activity in London. A moment of silence preceded the race and then came the best possible reaction to such atrocities – carrying on with normal daily life, which in our case means – running. Injury had taken our team down below the necessary four a couple of days earlier. The Skipper stepped into the breach, only to find that due to the transport shut-down he was not able to get to the start. An unfit Don Anderson promised to get round somehow but a tentative call was made to the Ward household to see if Richard was back from University – and if he was, had he done any running recently? The call came up trumps. Coincidentally he was in this neck of the woods, because the following day he was setting off for his brother’s stag “do” in Budapest. With only three hours warning it was Richard Ward to the rescue. The quest for our ninth consecutive win was on again. Very light rain started falling as Junior Galley set out on leg one. Epsom & Ewell led the field home with Guildford close up in second and the Bels in third, 28 seconds off the pace. The leading two teams switched places on the second circuit while Steve Zealey kept the Bels just about in striking distance, now 50 seconds behind. Stage three and it was Epsom’s turn to go ahead again, while some way back, “Wardy” skated the circuit perhaps a minute slower than he would if fit, but nevertheless closing on the leaders. The gap was still 38 seconds and a win seemed a lot to ask of Phil Wicks, only just recovering from illness. Organiser Dave Denton raised a quizzical eyebrow in the direction of our Team Manager – maybe the win streak was over. But Phil’s not keen on coming anything but first. In spite of a 24 second advantage, the Guildford man was caught after a little over half a mile of running and taking the right-angle bends wide to avoid slipping on the greasy surface, the Belgrave man began pulling the Epsom runner back as well. A mile out, on the grassy stretch, a Belgrave vest went ahead for the first time of the evening. It was all over, and from the look of young Phil at the race end, he was well over his illness and could no doubt have gone close to ten minutes in dry conditions. 1 Belgrave 44:37 (J Galley M40 11:25, S Zealey 11:43, R Ward 11:08, P Wicks 10:21); 2 Epsom & Ewell 45:03; 3 Guildford & Godalming 45:04; 50 teams finished. items.s: Different course, different challenger – same winner Report of the Surrey County 5 km at Wimbledon, won by Phil Wicks ahead of Hassan Raidi, with the Belgrave men winning the team title and the women's team taking county medals. Surrey County 5 km, Wimbledon, 14 August 2005. Hassan Raidi was back from a spell of training in Morocco where he had been getting himself into shape for the following week’s Auckland Castle 10 km, but on the tough Wimbledon course used by Surrey County for their 5km Championship he was unable to stop a rampant Phil Wicks from continuing his winning ways. The race starts in Cottenham Park Road and immediately climbs for 500 metres, taking in what we used to know as “the kiss of death” in our old 5 ¾ mile road race, until Christ Church on the corner of Copse Hill is reached. There was nothing much between the pair in the early stages, or when they strode out down Copse Hill, but when they turned near the bottom and entered Cottenham Park Road at the very bottom of the hill to begin the second ascent, Phil was showing signs of pulling away. At the end of the lap he was about 10 seconds clear but up by the church the gap had extended to around half a minute – and it grew. Lee Greatorex ran well to close in our winning men’s Surrey Championship team and we kept our grasp on the Surrey Road League as a result. The women’s team also featured in the county medals with Tilly Heaton leading the way and picking up individual bronze as well. She ended up as equal winner overall for the summer series. We also welcomed Heidi Cayzer into the team for the first time and look forward to seeing her at many more events in the future. items.label: No. 234
items.h: Marty makes waves at Bondi – beats veteran Steve Moneghetti
items.sum: Canberra Times report of Martin Dent finishing first Australian in the 2005 City to Surf in Sydney ahead of Steve Moneghetti, with an editor's footnote that Erwin McRae was 12th.
items.s: Marty makes waves at Bondi – beats veteran Steve Moneghetti Canberra Times report of Martin Dent finishing first Australian in the 2005 City to Surf in Sydney ahead of Steve Moneghetti, with an editor's footnote that Erwin McRae was 12th. He ran into a London fence two years ago, ran a marathon in Chicago last year and ran into the record books yesterday as the first Australian across the line in the 2005 City to Surf race in Sydney. Canberra’s Martin Dent conquered Heartbreak Hill and sprinted away from semi-retired Steve Moneghetti. However, the 26-year-old failed to drop defending champion Patrick Nyangelo or Dickson Marwa, who finished one-two for Tanzania in the 14km race. Only seven seconds separated Dent and Nyangelo, who claimed his third City to Surf victory. “The times were close,” Dent said. “But I think particularly the guy that won, he wasn’t flat out, I don’t think he was stretched out at all. He’s won the past two years, so it wasn’t a fluke.” Before the race, Dent said it would be a tough feat just to beat 43-year-old Moneghetti, who finished fourth, but hoped his youth would win out. “He’ll be a year older so maybe he might be a bit easier to beat.” After sharing the lead with the three-time Olympian, Dent broke away with the Africans as Moneghetti dropped off the pace on the 3km descent into Bondi Beach. “It’s good for Australian running. I think but someone had to beat him to stop the domination. When the best runners are 43 years old it’s a bit of a shame,” Dent said. While his finishing time was still adrift of Moneghetti’s race record 40min 03sec, Dent recorded 41:19 which was a one minute improvement on last year's performance and a personal best for the distance. “It wasn't easy,” Dent said. “I wasn’t really sure how I’d go so obviously it was a lot better than my expectations.” The City to Surf race was his first major competition since placing 13th in the Chicago Marathon last October. Having trained through a problematic Achilles injury for most of this year, Dent said he ran pain free yesterday. He also explained how such injuries can often be a blessing. “Having a break has been good as your body can fully recover from what you’ve done to it and sort of build up again stronger and faster. In the past I sometimes got a bit too obsessed with getting runs in, and running up to 180km a week, but lately I’ve been running as much as I’ve felt comfortable with.” Dent left his finance office on Friday as a policy advisor for the Australian Government, but will return today as a minor celebrity. “It's good for corporate recognition at work. You could come third at World Champs and everyone would be impressed obviously, but coming third in the City to Surf would be just as big for them.” However, there was no hope of Dent retiring to pursue a running career full-time as no prize money was offered for the event. “I got a trophy,” he said. Dent would also reward himself with an “easy week” of training before aiming to break the course record at Dunrissol Drive in the ACT Cross Country competition next weekend. Rebecca Wiasak, Canberra Times, Monday, 15 August 2005 Footnote: 12th in the City to Surf race was Erwin McRae in 43:52. Belgrave must have been within a whisker of winning the team event! items.sum: Profile of club President Gerry North: his early life in Blackpool, national cross country titles, joining Belgrave in 1962, international career, captaincy and later work in athletics.
items.s: The President – Gerry North Profile of club President Gerry North: his early life in Blackpool, national cross country titles, joining Belgrave in 1962, international career, captaincy and later work in athletics. At each AGM we honour a Belgrave Harrier by electing him or her President for the year. Last September Gerry North became the latest in a long line of Belgravians so honoured. Born in Chester, Cheshire on 1st May 1936, Gerry spent his early days living successively in Coventry and Wallasey before moving to Blackpool with his family, where his athletics career first took off. Although he has become something of an athletic legend in his own lifetime it is not so well known that that Gerry’s sporting aspirations could have taken a completely different path. He proved to be a very successful young footballer, playing for a youth team in Blackpool, alongside the likes of George Eastham and Jimmy Armfield (both of whom went on to become internationals). However, winning races at school and local level, at distances from a half mile upwards, had a distinct appeal to Gerry’s competitive nature and so running won the day. Leaving school at 15, he served his National Service in the Army from 1956 to 1958, after which he took employment with the Atomic Energy Authority near Preston. It was in 1958 that his name really came to the fore when he won the English National Junior Cross Country title, to be followed by the ‘Senior’ in 1962. Both titles came in the colours of Blackpool and Fylde A C. Following his success in the ‘National’ Gerry, joined Belgrave in the summer of 1962, to be followed by brother Geoff the following year, when his family moved south from Lancashire. Gerry became involved the Sports Sales business, with fellow international Stan Eldon. He soon integrated and absorbed himself into Belgrave life and went on to have an illustrious career as an international, representing Great Britain on the track, road and cross-country. Although competing at the highest-level Gerry always remained a real clubman and true Belgravian, moulded in the same image as some of our past legends such as Tom Carter, Arthur Penny and Bert Footer. During his active career Gerry lead our road and cross-country teams not only by example in his running, but also by enthusiasm and inspiration. Both Bill Lucas and Gordon Biscoe, the team managers during Gerry’s reign, have acknowledged his integrity and the important role he played as Team Captain during that period, and for which he was duly honoured with Life Membership. At the end of his active career Gerry moved to West Sussex, which took him out of the circle of everyday Belgrave life, but ‘you can’t keep a good man down’ and he was able to join forces with Portsmouth A C, playing a major role in their coaching, management and promotions. He continued to support us and visit us whenever possible, both at social events like the dinner dance, as well as at major championships such as the Southern and National CC and road relays etc. During 2003/2004 he willingly came on board with his acknowledge and expertise on road running, spending several days at Battersea Park and Crystal Palace, assisting in planning the courses for our Super Nova series of road races. Since retiring Gerry has involved himself in various areas of athletics administration an organisation. He has thus kept in touch with the modern scene and has very strong opinions as to how current athletics is being run! In 2003 Gerry was among many sportsmen and women nominated for honours in a ‘Sports Awards’ event promoted by the Portsmouth Evening News, and sponsored by several local businesses. There were numerous categories up for contention covering both individuals and teams, in sports ranging from netball to rifle shooting and football to synchronised swimming. Gerry’s success came in the ‘Grass Roots Award’ for his ‘Services to Athletics’. In a glowing tribute paid to him at the award ceremony, he was described as “eating, drinking and sleeping athletics.” He is known and respected by many throughout the UK and is truly a great ambassador not only for Belgrave but our Sport as a whole. Gordon Biscoe The International Cross Country Championships, Leopardstown Racecourse, Dublin, 21st March 1964. The Belgrave Cross Country Captain Gerry North, representing England, leads Jim Hogan of Polytechnic H & Ireland. They finished a fine 4th and 5th respectively. England won the race with 38 points from France, 96, and Morocco, 149. Gerry is pictured after his win in the Southern Counties AAA 6 miles track championship at Motspur Park on 25 April 1964. He won in 28:40.4, beating Ron Gomez of Southgate. items.sum: Club gossip: news from former youth athlete John Stow, a walker's chance reunion with his step cousin at the Ely 10km, and a photo of the Horwich RMI Clog Dancers at the Horwich Carnival.
items.s: Grapevine Club gossip: news from former youth athlete John Stow, a walker's chance reunion with his step cousin at the Ely 10km, and a photo of the Horwich RMI Clog Dancers at the Horwich Carnival. • A short while ago we heard from John Stow, a member of Belgrave Harriers as a young athlete through to senior status, 1968 until 1978. He is married now with three children – David, 20, Jacquie, 17 (and a hammer thrower), and Michael who is 13. John works for Aon in Romford. He recalls that in 1970 we had a very strong youth team that included Peter Carton, Bill Curtin, John himself and Tony Binda, with whom he still keeps in contact. These four won the Surrey Youths CC Championship twice, getting four runners in the first six on one occasion, and twice they were 2nd in the Southern and had a best National placing of 4th. They were coached by Ron Linstead. John is keen to make contact with those who remember him – in particular Colin Pearson, Brian Gorman, Gordon Biscoe and Reg Hopkins who was his team manager. John is now at Harlow AC, coaching twenty youngsters doing sprints and middle distance. He says “Hello,” to everyone and tells us that he loved his days at Belgrave and even today looks upon the Bels as his “main club”. • The Ely 10km was open to walkers and runners alike. During the race, inevitably some runners found it easier to walk and after about 8k one runner was encouraged, by a walker, to start running again just to keep warm. He moved away only to fall back after a few hundred metres. This happened twice more before the finish was reached. The runner thanked the walker, who had beaten him home, for keeping him moving – and that might have been the end of it. Not quite, however, as that evening the walker received a telephone call from the runner to thank him once again and to enquire whether he knew another walker by the name of Hall? The answer was that there were, or had been, several of that name, and when asked the reason for the enquiry the runner replied that his step cousin, of whom he had not heard for over 40 years, was Eric Hall. There was a stunned silence before Eric owned up to being one and the same person as had spoken to the runner. It is a very small world. The moral of this tale is, be kind to those you are passing as you never know who they are related to! Eric Hall, via Essex Walker Mike Blackledge captured what at first was thought to be a protest after the result of the AAA 5km at Horwich was announced. The Horwich Carnival Parade was led by … a group of men dressed in claret and gold, dancing about and aggressively waving sticks! But no, it wasn’t Miles, Anderson & Co. venting their frustration at being pipped by Salford Harriers – it was the world famous Horwich RMI Clog Dancers. We liked the claret caps with gold tassels but felt the velvet shorts and gold sashes might not be suitable for cross-country. items.sum: Panel of facts about Gerry North's career, with his championship titles, international appearances, best performances and his current posts in athletics.
items.s: Gerry’s athletic career – some facts Panel of facts about Gerry North's career, with his championship titles, international appearances, best performances and his current posts in athletics. • Gerry is the only person to have achieved the triple of becoming National Cross Country Champion as a Junior (1958), as a Senior (1962) and as a Veteran (1986). • He ran for England in the International CC Championships (now the World Championship) six times, scoring in the winning team five times (15th in 1960, 8th in 1962, 4th in 1964, 12th in 1965 and 19th in 1966. • Gerry was twice the winner of the Inter-Counties CC (1960, 1962), • won the Northern CC title three times, the Southern CC title once, the Lancashire Senior CC title three times, the Surrey CC title four times. • On the track Gerry won both the Northern and Southern Six Miles Championships. • In the days when the Southern and National Road Relay Champions were held over the London-Brighton course, Gerry set the record of 28:29 for stage 8 – the longest stage. • His main career spanned eleven years from 1954 to 1964 and during this period he ran 359 track races and 258 road or cross country races – an average of more than one race per week! • Gerry continued to run as a veteran until the age of 50 when he won the Vets National CC title (he is rumoured to be currently planning a comeback – aged 65!) items.sum: Profile of Belgrave race walker Maureen Noel, who won the combined women's Southern and National 50 km walk title at her debut at the distance, tracing her progress since 2002 and her marathon running.
items.s: Maureen Noel – Fast Lady! Profile of Belgrave race walker Maureen Noel, who won the combined women's Southern and National 50 km walk title at her debut at the distance, tracing her progress since 2002 and her marathon running. Relatively new to the sport, Maureen Noel (pictured left) can already point to a National Race Walking title over 50km – and a 3:29 marathon. We have the feeling that there is a lot more to come. John Hall tells us more:- Maureen won the combined women’s Southern and National 50 kilometre walking championships at Earls Colne in Essex on Sunday 4th September in hot conditions. It was her debut at the distance and, considering the heat and the fact that she suffered bad blistering to her feet in the closing stages, her time of 6 hours 2 minutes and 53 seconds was very respectable. And considering she had done very little training beforehand her performance augurs very well for future efforts over the distance. Maureen has been in Belgrave colours for about two years. She was “discovered” three years ago when she competed in the Defra (Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs) Sports Day. Without any training she did every track event from 100 metres to 3,000 metres and among the trophies she picked up was one for the second highest points score for a woman. Maureen said she had always wanted to be an athlete but hadn’t known how to get involved. Waiting to your late 30’s to get started may be a bit extreme, but better late than never…. Among the events she did that day in June 2002 was the 2,000 metres walk. Maureen had never tried race walking before but her performance was good enough to prompt John Hall to invite her to join him for training. He entered her for her second race, the 3,000 metres walk in the Civil Service track and field championships at Wigan 7 weeks later, and the rest, as they say….. Maureen finished second in 20 minutes 3.7 seconds and has progressed since then to get her time down to 17:31. However, short distances aren’t Maureen’s forte. The people who regularly beat her at 3,000 and 5,000 metres walk find her powering past them in the later stages of races from about 10k upwards. So she has won the Middlesex 10 mile title this year and 6 days later won the Southern 20k. And her 10k track time is faster than doubling her best 5k time! Running still holds attractions for Maureen. She continues to run everything from 100 metres upwards at the annual Defra sports and at the Civil Service veterans championships and can’t resist a couple of runs at the main CS championships – after all a 3,000 metres walk doesn’t take much out of her so why not use some surplus energy… Seeing the London Marathon, Maureen declared an interest in running it. First John Hall trained with her for the Luton Marathon, which incorporated the Civil Service championship, in December 2004. John ran with Maureen and kept her from going too fast in the first half of the race. At about 15 miles, as he ran out of steam, he encouraged Maureen to run on ahead. She obliged by finishing 13 minutes ahead, in 3:38. Not bad on modest training. The London Marathon followed, with even less running training but an improved time (3:29). What Maureen needs now is some consistent training and proper coaching and we may really see what she can achieve. Above: Maureen Noel, pictured during the 10k track walk at Battersea Park back in April by Jeremy Hemming. items.sum: Report and results of the Auckland Castle 10 km incorporating the AAA and CAU Inter-County championships, where Belgrave men were second in the AAA team race and the women third.
items.s: Pipped by Morpeth again Report and results of the Auckland Castle 10 km incorporating the AAA and CAU Inter-County championships, where Belgrave men were second in the AAA team race and the women third. Road Running Auckland Castle 10km inc. AAA & CAU Inter-County Champs., 21 August 2005. The long haul to the North East for the Auckland Castle and AAA 10k, closely co-operating with the Surrey team for the Inter-County race, was another enjoyable experience. Once again the men were just pipped for the AAA team race and it was silver again - our fourth consecutive year as medallists. The Belles were also into the hardware, gaining a surprising set of bronze awards. And with both our teams heavily involved in the scoring for the Inter-County titles, there were yet more medals as the Surrey men placed 3rd and the women 2nd. We like winning, of course, but one of the most pleasing thing these days is that we ride our bad luck and still make a great contribution to the race. Birhan Dagne was unable to stay the course, coming out at 4k, David Anderson is continually troubled by his Achilles tendon problem and was another dnf (can’t say we ever remember that happening before) while Mark Miles was unable to start due to a tendon problem of his own. But for these misfortunes it could have been double team win. The men's team race was so tight that had it been calculated on accumulated times, as many races are these days, we would have won - exactly the same situation as with the AAA 5k a month or so earlier. Of course some other time this type of scoring could work to our advantage, but looking at the women’s team results one can see that the team places were calculated on actual race positions - including men, guests, overseas competitors, etc. Where so many categories are included within the one event, accumulated times have got to be the fairest way of doing things. items.sum: Report and results of the Surrey County AA Road Relays at Wimbledon Park, where Belgrave men were second and the women fourth overall and third in the Surrey Championship.
items.s: Team Manager in the medals Report and results of the Surrey County AA Road Relays at Wimbledon Park, where Belgrave men were second and the women fourth overall and third in the Surrey Championship. Surrey County AA Road Relays, Wimbledon Park, 10 September 2005. This year’s event was switched to the nearby bowls pavilion because Wimbledon Park athletic track was closed for refurbishment; as a result the course was a little longer than normal. After a long run of silver medals in the Surrey Relay our men’s team had the chance to go for a hat-trick of wins, having won in 2003 and 2004 – but it was back to the runners-up slot once more as alternative events took precedence in our runners’ diaries. Lee Greatorex is aiming to tackle the longer distances and his extra mileage seems to be giving him a boost over the shorter road runs as well. His fourth on the opening leg was converted to second place on leg two by the Skipper, who interrupted his support of the England cricket team by cycling from the Oval Cricket Ground to Wimbledon to do his bit – and then cycling back again for the after tea session. Only the non-scoring Thames team was ahead at this point and they were caught by Knut Hegvold on stage three, but South London’s Jason Simpson also came through and with a strong trio to follow, it was left to our own Messrs Ellacott, Humphrey and Browne to hold on to second spot as SLH gained a stranglehold on the race. With M40s, M50s W35s and Senior Women racing at the same time as the men but over just four stages it can be very difficult to work out what is going on. Heidi Cayzer gave us a solid start and then Rosie Powell moved up two places to fourth. Team Manager Catherine Eastham put her clipboard and team sheet aside to keep the Belles in the hunt and with Jules surging through on the last stage we came home fourth – and third in the Surrey Championship as Epsom’s outstanding Emily Nelson had run twice in her club’s team, thus ruling them ineligible. items.s: Flashback - 1960 1960 photograph of Surrey's record-setting women's sprint relay team at the Inter-County Championship, including Marianne Dew, later Belgrave's Marianne Black. Flashback - 1960 Pictured above is Surrey’s sprint relay team which set a record in the Women’s Inter-County Championship. From left to right they are Jennifer Taylor (Mitcham AC), Marianne Dew (Selsonia LAC), Mary Hall (Hercules AC) and Janet Neil (Mitcham AC). Of course Marianne Dew is none other than our own Marianne Black. Photo by Gerry Cranham. items.sum: Short piece, credited to Essex Walker, welcoming the IAAF's doubling of drug bans from two to four years and contrasting American baseball's leniency.
items.s: Drug rule changes Short piece, credited to Essex Walker, welcoming the IAAF's doubling of drug bans from two to four years and contrasting American baseball's leniency. Sport’s incessant war against drugs took a tentative pace forward when the IAAF voted to step up the suspension of convicted athletes from 2-to-4 years. Most genuine athletes would like it see it raised to ‘for life’. If it was ‘for life’ human rights lawyers representing the star athletes so banned would immediately be citing ‘restraint of trade’. That’s life nowadays. However the IAAF must still be commended for doubling the ban. And the most lenient sport for drug takers? That’s American baseball, where those caught rattling with steroids are confined to their dug-outs for precisely 4 weeks! From Essex Walker

items.sum: Review of Belgrave's 2005 British Athletics League season, in which the club failed to win a ninth consecutive Division One title, with the table of individual BAL points scores.
items.s: British League Performances in 2005 Review of Belgrave's 2005 British Athletics League season, in which the club failed to win a ninth consecutive Division One title, with the table of individual BAL points scores. Time heals, so they say. And whilst reflecting on the track season just passed, and in particular on our failure to hold on at the top of the British Athletics League, the first stirrings of an urge to regain our title are becoming very much stronger. It will be a difficult task and we will most certainly need some huge commitment from our athletes. But in the meantime, let’s take stock of the guys that earned the points in 2005. Bill Laws tells us: Generally we need between 55 and 57 athletes to provide a league winning effort over four matches. This year we only managed to get 50 to the starting line and that proved insufficient to secure a ninth consecutive Division One victory. On the face of it competition from other meetings had depleted our teams but it could be argued that this affected all teams so that was not the main problem. A closer analysis of the 57 athletes who turned out last season showed that 23 did not make it this year. So we blooded 16 new members and relied heavily on our older hands. William Sharman claimed top spot on his own this year as only he, Mick Jones and new member Adrian Phillips made all four matches. There will be some serious revisions to the all time points scores table as many of our big points scorers continued to rack up impressive contributions to the team’s efforts. items.s: George French Trophy News item: Tony Fairclough received the George French Trophy for 2004 on Belgrave's behalf, awarded to the club scoring highest in all AAA track and field championships. News On behalf of Belgrave Harriers, Tony Fairclough (pictured above) took charge of the George French Trophy, presented by UKA Performance Director Dave Collins at Bedford on 3rd July 2005 for the year 2004. The trophy is awarded to the club scoring highest in all AAA T&F competitions, men and women, indoors and out, and including multi-events. Belgrave have won this trophy each year since 2000 – but will we win it for 2005? – there were a lot of Woodford Green with Essex Ladies vests prominent at this year’s championships. items.h: Tim Benjamin - 6th on UK all-time list
items.sum: Reprinted report, credited to BT Yahoo, on Tim Benjamin's second place to Tyree Washington in Monaco in a Belgrave record 44.56 for 400 metres, sixth on the UK all-time list.
items.s: Tim Benjamin - 6th on UK all-time list Reprinted report, credited to BT Yahoo, on Tim Benjamin's second place to Tyree Washington in Monaco in a Belgrave record 44.56 for 400 metres, sixth on the UK all-time list. Tim Benjamin is glad his summer season has finally come to an end despite the success he has enjoyed over 400metres. Benjamin was runner-up to Tyree Washington in a thrilling one-lap encounter in Monaco and his time capped an outstanding couple of months. “I’m tired and really looking forward to taking a break,” said Benjamin when it was suggested he is running so well it might be a good idea to take in another couple of races. American Washington, a former world indoor champion, lunged at the finishing line to earn a winner's purse of £16,312 when it looked likely Benjamin would pick up a first major global title. With four men, including Olympic and world champion Jeremy Wariner in contention for the top prize, Washington set a season’s best to beat Benjamin by 0.05 seconds in their knife-edge encounter. The pair and Chris Brown were virtually inseparable until Washington clinched it as Benjamin, who clocked 44.56secs, (a Belgrave record) held off the Bahamian by 0.08secs. Wariner would have been with them until knocked out of his stride pattern when he and Benjamin, in the lane outside him, had a contact of hands halfway up the final straight. Benjamin lowering his personal best for the fifth time in the last two months said: “I thought I had it won and it cost me 10K - it was so close. Judging by that I can run 0.25secs quicker,” which would put him within sight of fellow Welshman Iwan Thomas’ British record. Benjamin feels he can match the European gold medal Thomas won seven years ago when Gothenburg hosts the championship next season. He said: “Now I am running so fast, I just hope I can continue to do so next season.” From BT Yahoo Tim Benjamin Tim Benjamin 2nd 400m IAAF World Athletics Final, Monaco, 44.56 (Belgrave record), 6th on UK all-time list Tim Benjamin Benjamin Tyree Washington Tyree Washington American; won 400m in Monaco Tyree Washington Washington Jeremy Wariner Jeremy Wariner Olympic and world champion Jeremy Wariner Wariner Chris Brown Chris Brown the Bahamian Iwan Thomas Iwan Thomas British 400m record holder; European gold medal Iwan Thomas Thomas IAAF World Athletics Final European Championships Monaco Gothenburg

items.label: No. 235
items.sum: News item on Paul Freary, who after recovering from injury ran in the Great Russian Run but was then hit by a car before the Rufford 10km.
items.s: Paul Freary's jinx strikes again! News item on Paul Freary, who after recovering from injury ran in the Great Russian Run but was then hit by a car before the Rufford 10km. Having recovered from the trapped nerve in his neck - after months of agony and no training - Paul Freary gradually got into reasonable shape only for a calf muscle to twang in his first race back. Gradually he got over that problem and became fit enough to take part in The Great Russian Run - Vladivostok to St. Petersburg. The Russian run went really well with his section of 86 miles being covered in six days. So it was back to the UK to spend the next three weeks getting ready for the SEAA 6-Stage. But that jinx stepped in again. On Sunday 4 September he was about to run in the Rufford 10km but while leaning through the sliding door of his van, just before the race, he was hit by a passing car. Paul went to Chorley Hospital where it was decided that nothing was broken but he ended up with some almighty bruising from his hips to his heels, with tyre marks down the backs of his legs. We think we can safely say that he was actually very lucky that it wasn’t more serious. Anyway, his last three weeks before the SEAA race began with a spell of inactivity while he recovered. Paul does still intend to race at Rushmoor Arena so we wish him a speedy recovery. items.h: Double gold for Harry in World Youth Games
items.sum: Reprinted report, credited to BT Yahoo, on Harry Aikines-Aryeetey becoming the first sprinter to win both 100 and 200 metres gold at the World Youth Championships, in a world-leading 20.91 for 200m.
items.s: Double gold for Harry in World Youth Games Reprinted report, credited to BT Yahoo, on Harry Aikines-Aryeetey becoming the first sprinter to win both 100 and 200 metres gold at the World Youth Championships, in a world-leading 20.91 for 200m. Harry Aikines-Aryeetey – the Sutton & District AC man who also races for Belgrave Harriers – became the first sprinter in the six-year history of the IAAF/Maroc Telecom World Youth Championships ever to win both the 100 and 200 metres gold medals. The 16-year-old, having won the shorter race title on Thursday 14 July, powered to another magnificent victory over 200m in his final on Sunday night. Aikines-Aryeetey turned the tables on Cuba’s Jorge Valcarcel, who was given the verdict in their semi-final although both had finished with the same time. In the final, the Sutton/Belgrave sprinter showed he was the better man, controlling the race from start to finish and winning in a world leading time for the year of 20.91seconds. His pace saw him easily overthrow the challenge of Valcarcel and Matteo Galvan of Italy, although both rivals ran personal best times of 21.08sec and 21.14sec. “I just can’t believe it,” said Aikines-Aryeetey who after raising his hand with a number one finger salute, spent a couple of minutes flat-out on his back after his outstanding performance. “I just can't believe it, I was lying on my back on the floor before it really dawned I was world champion yet again.” The win saw him become the second British champion over the distance, following in the footsteps of 1999 winner Tim Benjamin who is now carving out an international career over 400 metres. “I've no idea,” said Aikines-Aryeetey when asked where he found the energy to run the fastest half lap of his life after six demanding races in five days. He added: “Yesterday I was a bit tired but felt a lot better today. I ran a quick bend and I didn't really see anyone. “My coach had told me hit the first 120 hard which I did. Then I saw the the Cuban alongside and just drove even harder. “It’s just amazing. I had so much lactic, I knew I was going to do something special and I just can’t believe it that I ran 20.91 seconds.” Aikines-Aryeetey, who beat 21 seconds for the first time in his career, has been so focused on his preparations he was unaware that no-one had ever before achieved the demanding sprint double. “I suppose I’ve made history,” said last year’s Commonwealth Youth Games runner-up. “But yes, I’ve got to be happy with two medals – who’d have thought it?” From BT Yahoo Harry Aikines-Aryeetey Harry Aikines-Aryeetey won 100m and 200m gold at World Youth Championships 2005, 200m in 20.91 Harry Aikines-Aryeetey Aikines-Aryeetey Harry Jorge Valcarcel Jorge Valcarcel Cuba; 21.08 in 200m final Jorge Valcarcel Valcarcel Matteo Galvan Matteo Galvan Italy; 21.14 in 200m final Tim Benjamin Tim Benjamin 1999 World Youth 200m winner World Youth Championships Commonwealth Youth Games Sutton & District AC

items.h: Brad Poore features in the San Francisco Cable Car Chase
items.sum: News item on Brad Poore finishing second in the ANA Cable Car Chase in San Francisco and his hope to study at law school in England.
items.s: Brad Poore features in the San Francisco Cable Car Chase News item on Brad Poore finishing second in the ANA Cable Car Chase in San Francisco and his hope to study at law school in England. Taking a little time out from studying, Brad Poore gave his Belgrave kit another airing, racing in the the ANA Cable Car Chase, in San Francisco. It was an incredibly hard course including some of the biggest hills in San Francisco. The course was 5.67 miles and after two flat, fast miles he took the lead on the main big hill and broke away to gain a 20 meters advantage by the summit. He was still leading with about 1.5 miles remaining but on the downhills got overtaken by Jason Balkman (23:11 or so last year in the USA 8k Championships). Brad ended up getting second place in 28:54 and won a trip for two to Los Angeles (flights, hotels, and Disneyland passes included!). First place would have been a trip to Tokyo though! Brad is hoping to come to England next August/September and do a semester at law school. The problem is trying to find a law school that has an exchange program with any USA (ABA approved) law school that also has a decent running program. Does anyone have any ideas and/or contacts? items.sum: Look back at club news from 1980: Carl Lawton becoming President, Tom Carter's 50 years as a Belgravian, Ernie Obeng's sprinting, junior rankings and the South of England 12-Stage Road Relay.
items.s: From The Belgravian – 25 Years Ago – 1980 Look back at club news from 1980: Carl Lawton becoming President, Tom Carter's 50 years as a Belgravian, Ernie Obeng's sprinting, junior rankings and the South of England 12-Stage Road Relay. From The Belgravian 25 Years Ago – 1980 Carl Lawton took over from Bill Merryman as President of Belgrave Harriers … Bill Laws edited The Belgravian while Alan Mead was Track & Field Secretary. The club magazine cost around £300 per issue to produce in those days (it was to rise to nearly ten times that by the time it had became a glossy A4 publication – but in it’s current downloadable format it is virtually free). In August Tom Carter celebrated 50 years as a Belgravian. The magazine reported, “ There are few men who have obtained international honours and given a lifetime to encouraging the endeavours of others.” A surprise party was held at the Hall and pride of place was given to a fine cake decorated with a faithful replica of the Belgrave’s badge. Derek Jones completed his first year as Secretary of the Women’s Section – the team placed 5th in Division III (South) of the Southern League. Ernie Obeng (now an employee of the IAAF in Monaco) kept the name of Belgrave Harriers on sports commentator’s lips as he reeled off a succession of 100 metre sprint wins at stadiums all over the world. Although denied the chance of competing at Moscow (in the Olympic Games) due to organisational problems in his home country of Ghana, he must have been considered a potential medallist over the short sprint. For not only did he beat Cuba’s Silvio Leonard, subsequently the silver medallist, just a few weeks before the Games, he also defeated Allan Wells, the Olympic Champion, shortly after Moscow. His best time of 10.21 was a club record. Junior John Gladwin topped the club rankings at 800 metres (1:48.7) and 1500m (3:52.9) and fellow under 20 Stuart Paton’s name was found at the top of the 3000 metres list with 8:34.0. Belgrave placed 15th in the South of England 12-Stage Road Relay held at Wimbledon in conjunction with The Belgrave Haig Relay. Highlight of the race was the devastating run by Steve Ovett who took Brighton & Hove from 7th to 1st and smashed the short stage record. items.h: Brian Pritchard – President of Belgrave Harriers 2005-6
items.sum: Gordon Biscoe's profile of new club President Brian Pritchard, a member since 1942, followed by a message from Brian himself and a plug for the club Dinner & Dance.
items.s: Brian Pritchard – President of Belgrave Harriers 2005-6 Gordon Biscoe's profile of new club President Brian Pritchard, a member since 1942, followed by a message from Brian himself and a plug for the club Dinner & Dance. Brian joined Belgrave on the 5th September 1942 at the age of 4! He was signed up by his enthusiastic father, who also had two brothers running for the Club. Brian was obviously expected to run and compete, which he did as a young boy, but after not achieving much success he rebelled, as youngsters do, and somewhat faded from the scene although remaining a keen supporter. He recalls occasions standing on the Common or at the side of the roads watching races with Mavis Hall. His father being a great friend of her father Tom Morrell. It was not until after his father had died, that Brian returned to the fold and, as his own children came along and wanted to compete, that he became more and more involved, and has remained so ever since. Over the years Brian has had many roles within the Club. For several years he assisted Ron Wyld in looking after the youngsters, acting as team manager, organiser and transport officer all in one! Then, when Ron emigrated to Australia, he continued on his own, covering both road, track and cross country. Among some of his squad during this period were Andrew North, Mark Sinclair and John Gladwin, who claims his first run for Belgrave was with Brian. Brian’s interests also included ‘Walking’, attending various meetings when his daughter Jayne, who had the honour of being the first lady to join Belgrave, took up competitive walking. On the Social side he has run numerous Socials and Discos at the Hall, organised ‘Surrey Suppers’ for Surrey County AA at the Hall, assisted Bill Couzens in organising the Dinner Dance (including the Centenary Year), and on several occasions travelled around with Bill vetting various Bands they thought might be appropriate to book. He has been a great supporter the Club at all levels of competition, attending not only National, Area and County events on the Road and Country as well as British League Meetings but also Club events at Battersea Park and Wimbledon Common, etc. For many years he has been only too willing to respond to the call for officials or course markers, helping out in all weathers. Some three years ago he took over the organisation of the annual Club dinner dance, and in spite of a spell in hospital involving major surgery, he has revitalised it to the continuing popular event that it is today. Thus, with some 63 years of Club service and a wealth of experience behind him, Brian can be described as a true Belgravian. We look forward to his year as President. Gordon Biscoe … and a few lines from Brian … … Just to say how honoured and privileged I am to be asked to be your President for the coming year. My father Thomas Pritchard joined the Club in the 1930’s and in later years became a Life Member of Belgrave so I am especially pleased to carry on the tradition. I have a daughter, two sons, a grandaughter and a grandson Thomas who are also members of Belgrave. Thomas is a fourth generation Belgravian which is especially pleasing as our family name will hopefully carry on in the Club for many years to come. During my years in Belgrave I have made some wonderful friendships that have endured over the decades and I can honestly say that not being very gifted as a runner has never been a hindrance as I have always been made to feel at home in this great Club of ours. In closing I would just like to wish everybody the very best for the coming year and will try to get to see as many of you as I can while I am President. Yours Brian Pritchard PS A plug for the club Dinner & Dance at Reigate Manor Hotel on the 26th November 2005. It would be nice to see as many of you there as possible as I am sure you will have a good evening. Guest speaker this year will be David Bedford. If you need tickets please phone me on [phone number withheld]. items.label: No. 236
items.sum: The Hon. Secretary's report to the 2005 AGM reviewing the club's year: deaths of Arthur Penstone and John Jeffery, the Sutton partnership, road and cross-country titles, women's, walkers' and juniors' seasons, loss of the British League title and outstanding individuals.
items.s: Hon Secretary’s Report to AGM 2005 The Hon. Secretary's report to the 2005 AGM reviewing the club's year: deaths of Arthur Penstone and John Jeffery, the Sutton partnership, road and cross-country titles, women's, walkers' and juniors' seasons, loss of the British League title and outstanding individuals. It has been quite a bittersweet year for our club with notable success mixed with sadness and some painful defeats. However, although club athletics in this country is at an uncertain crossroads, Belgravians can trust that their club is in robust health and that we can look to the future with confidence and optimism. The securing of London’s Olympic bid has boosted our profile, and people often look to us first when taking up athletics and joining a club. Our reputation is greater than ever, and stretches far. When a Polish athlete, his sister and father vacationed in London last week, my house was, naturally, their first port of call. Could he do some high jumps for Belgrave on his visit to England? Season over, I had to dash his dreams but it was still a telling moment. We were saddened by the death of Arthur Penstone this year whose most notable contribution to club life was the care and attention he devoted to Belgrave Hall. For about 50 years Arthur’s expertise as an electrician and handyman ensured the Hall remained in good condition. The club was also devastated to learn of the death of our friend, committee member, past-president and British League manager, John Jeffery. John worked tirelessly for the club in so many areas and we owe a lot of our recent success, prestige and reputation to him. We all miss him dearly, none more so than Bill Laws, John’s great friend and co-British League manager. Bill has now managed the team for a stunning 25 years in which he has dragged us from the bottom of the pile to many years of national dominance. At the end of the season Bill at first spoke of possibly taking a step back. Whatever you decide Bill, I should like to thank you on behalf of all of us for a quarter of a Century of tireless work. We set up a partnership with Sutton & District AC this year whereby, in track and field, certain Sutton athletes may now compete for Belgrave and, to a lesser extent, vice versa. We field composite Junior and Young Athletes Teams and officials of both clubs also get together to assist in the running of the meetings of either club. Belgrave Harriers used Sutton Arena for the first time for home meetings. On the field of play, last winter was highly rewarding for the road and cross-country section of the club with our members travelling the length and breadth of the country in search of silverware and often finding it. Our men struck gold six times and came second in four other high-profile events. We own all four major road-relay titles, and regained the prestigious National 12-stage title with a team of breath-taking depth and quality. I wonder how many other clubs in the world could have troubled us on that day. Our cross-country results were solid but after the wonderful win at the National in 2004, I detect a little underperformance, and our 8th and 6th places at the Southern and National were rather a shame, but, remember, a few short years ago we would have been ecstatic with such returns. Closer to home we were happy to reclaim the South of the Thames Championship. Our women now have almost every cog in place for an assault on titles of their own. The most important cog is imperiously in place, as in Catherine Eastham the women boast a team manager every bit as inspirational, thorough and determined as what the men enjoy. Some brief highlights include placing second at the Southern six-stage relay, defending their title at the Reigate Priory relay and a terrific 12th place at the National cross. They almost won the Surrey cross-country League but were just pipped in a dramatic final race by Ranelagh. In track and field our women, expertly guided by Cynthia James and Bob Bridges, were undefeated in division 4 of the UK League, and march to division 3 from where we hope again to win promotion. Our male track and field team finally had to relinquish our British League title after a terrific battle with Woodford Green. Nine titles in a row was not to be, but all credit to Woodford who have been nipping at our heels for several seasons now and fully deserved their win. We appeared to be particularly fallible in the sprinting events this year which is unusual for us, but our luck was definitely out with a whole group of the speedsters out of form, injured or competing elsewhere at the same time. In the Jubilee Cup we had one of those really dire days that sneak up uninvited every few years and failed to qualify for the final, as Rugby pipped us by two points. It has been a quiet year for our walkers as they linger near the bottom of the slope with an aim to get back up again. We are still turning out teams for the local events and competing regularly. Unfortunately, we have no class performers these days, apart from our 2nd claim member Estle Viljoen who spent much of last year off injured but who has now regained form to recently take 2nd place in the National 20kms. Our second lady walker, Maureen Noel completed the London Marathon (running) and recently won the National 50kms. Paul King our long distance performer completed the Colchester 100 last year and more recently the Kings Lynn 100 and was 4th in this year’s National 50kms. The icon that is Carl Lawton finished more races than anyone else in the country last year. Our juniors are often the victim of their own success with our best athletes on international duty during league matches. Consequently the junior men were relegated from the Southern premier division and join the Brent League. However, our junior girls won the Brent League and new rules dictate our boys and girls will now perform as a joint team in that league next summer. This is all much more convenient and suits us well. In my list of outstanding individual athletes over the past year, special mentions should go to the following: Mark Miles placed a tremendous 3rd in the National cross; Harry Aikines-Ayreetey won both the 100 and 200-metres at the World Youth Games in Marrakesh; Wade Bennett-Jackson was 2nd in the 100-metres at the Norwich Union Grand Prix under-20 race; and Chris Gearing continues to show great promise in the shot and recently won the UK Challenge Final to go with his win at the Inter-counties Under-20 event. Javelin thrower Goldie Sayers placed twelfth in the World Championships and fourth in the World Student Games; while Birhan Dagne, our national cross-country champion from 2004 continues to shine in road races all over the country. Finally, and most excitingly, in Tim Benjamin we could have the next big thing in British athletics. After placing 5th at the World Championships, Tim has just lowered our club 400-metre record to 44:56 in Monaco, to put him within a couple of tenths of Iwan Thomas’s British record, which Roger Black feels Tim will one day smash. In closing, our merry band of committee members and officials are working as hard as ever to ensure the club runs smoothly and that we continue to offer our members terrific value. All of our officials give up their time for free of course and deserve our humble gratitude: it is sobering to compare us for instance with the golf club I play at, which spent £323,000 on administration expenses last year. No such luxury for us, but if there’s ever anything you’d like to know about how you can assist or volunteer with the running of the club, don’t hesitate to let us know. The Belgrave story is now 118 years old and there’s no reason why the club can’t celebrate its 125th, 150th and 200th anniversaries as one of the great organizations in British sport. Thank you. items.label: No. 236
items.h: Bels rampant at Rushmoor – a fourth successive win
items.sum: Stage-by-stage report of Belgrave's fourth successive win at the SEAA 6 Stage road relay championship at Rushmoor Arena, Aldershot, on 24 September 2005, with team results, Belgrave splits and fastest legs.
items.s: Bels rampant at Rushmoor – a fourth successive win Stage-by-stage report of Belgrave's fourth successive win at the SEAA 6 Stage road relay championship at Rushmoor Arena, Aldershot, on 24 September 2005, with team results, Belgrave splits and fastest legs. Road & Country Aldershot Road Relays - SEAA 6 Stage Championship, Rushmoor Arena, 24 September 2005. We’ve had some thrills around the circuit at Rushmoor Arena in the past few years but this race was anticipated with more than the normal frisson of excitement. First of all, only two of last year’s winning team were in the ‘A’ six – Jonathan Blackledge and Stephen Sharp. A run of colds, varying degrees of Achilles tendon problems, a holiday in Mexico and an alternate race had taken out a famous five that might have made the cut – Kevin Nash, Adam Zawadski, Mark Miles, David Anderson and Hassan Raidi. For sixth man much thought was given to the choice between Paul Freary (an amazing run of times around Rushmoor and fit again after a year out with various injuries) and Al Stewart (another with a long period out but now running well and with an ok run at Bishop Auckland under his belt). Just 40 hours before the race Al got the nod but both were to run on the opening leg. Throw in the fact that 19-year old super-talent Shukri Omar was going to start the ‘C’s and we had a first stage battle to savour. Then there was the possibility that a Belgrave win could set an outright record for consecutive victories – Southampton City won three times ’93-’95 with our own hat trick being ’02-’04; but that victory was by no means assured as our own camp felt that Newham & Essex Beagles might have the edge. Wells City Harriers are also on the rise while Harrow were rumoured to have a strong outfit. Finally, ‘B’ teams would be eligible for the National race for the first time ever – if they could place in the top 20 here on the Army training grounds. Stage 1 The starter’s gun sent eighty-seven bodies on their way on the stroke of 2:30pm. Each stage of 6k is made up of two laps and as the first circuit was completed Hennessy of Wells City Harriers and Chinanhua of Poole had gained about 30 metres on the pack where sparks were flying as Al Stewart marginally led from Paul Freary with Shukri almost alongside – we had three men in the leading seven tearing lumps out of each other. Al imperceptibly began to move away going into the second lap with “Shugs” – not cleared to run in our scoring teams until 1st November – hanging on to him. Al Stewart was a revelation. He’d been picked on the basis of certainly being able to give us an 18:30 but as the second lap unwound he went from strength to strength. He caught the Poole runner near the gravel slope and by 500 metres to go was very close to the lead. Simons of Cornwall AC had been tracking our man, however, and sprinted past near the end to narrowly take the stage while Al caught the Wells City man to go into second. Paul Freary suffered on that second lap but has now made a huge stride back to fitness while Shukri gave the ‘C’s an awesome start. ‘A’s 2nd, ‘C’s 6th and ‘B’s 13th! Stage 2 It wasn’t supposed to be like this! A nice 10th place would have given Phil Wicks some men to chase in his quest for something around an 18:15 clocking; but here he was taking over just a second down on leaders Cornwall AC with Wells City a further second behind him. A quick shuffle and it was Wells from Belgrave as the Cornish team slipped back (Dave Buzza had already led his veterans’ team to silver medals) and Morris of Wells City took up the pace. Young Phil was biding his time though and soon eased ahead and away. Gradually stretching the gap he ended up well inside his target time and our lead was just under half a minute. Seventeen year-old Kris Gauson picked off several men for the ‘B’s to move into 10th – but they were still behind the non-scoring ‘C’s, holding on to 7th through Andrew Swearman. Stage 3 Spare a thought here for Tim Weeks in the ‘C’s – two weeks without running due to illness and here he was right near the front end of the field. An elite triathlete until a bad crash in Australia while training on his bike left him with a shattered leg, Tim has set himself the task of working his way into our top teams. Seven men including the Skipper came past and our team order was made sensible – ‘B’s 9th, ‘C’s 14th and ‘A’s 1st and storming away thanks to Tim Watson. Our lead was now 45 seconds over Wells City with Kent AC up to 3rd through Jermain Mays. Stage 4 Mo’ Farah was wheeled out now for Newham & Essex Beagles and soon he was rocketing through the field on his way to a 17:23 – the day’s fastest but some way behind the incredible course record of 17:07 by Brighton’s Andy Bristow from 1989. The Beagles came up ten places but there was no change at the front as Spencer Barden equalled his best ever time for the circuit – 17:54. Twenty-three year old Peter Willis made his first appearance in a Belgrave team – the ‘C’s – and exactly equalled the time set by Knut Hegvold in the ‘B’s; more young blood for the cross-country season ahead. Stage 5 Jonathan Blackledge was a little disappointed with his time on stage five but with the race coming earlier this year he was only just out of his end-of-season break. Nevertheless our lead now reached its maximum – we had gone away on every stage and now were 1:28 to the good. Once again our ‘B’ and ‘C’ runners clocked identical times – Lee Greatorex and Joachim Wolf ensuring now that we were going to achieve all that we had set out to do. Stage 6 ... And so to the finish, with a team time half a minute better than our best from 2003. Stephen Sharp had been itching for another sub-18 run but with no one to chase he had to do no more than go through the motions. Rumour has it that he is now employing Securicor to look after his home as he has 16 SEAA and AAA team “golds” plus 2 “silvers” in his trophy cabinet! Also on the last leg, John Clarke had handed his mobile phone to the team manager with the words, “my wife’s about to give birth in 8 minutes time – could you answer any calls while I'm out there.” As he cruised through the first of his laps we were able to let our ‘B’ anchor man know that there was no news from the maternity ward – dedicated men these Belgravians. Tenth place for the ‘B’s gave us great pleasure as we now had two teams qualified for Sutton Coldfield – and when Jason Webb closed in the ‘C’s, also inside the top 20 and only 17 seconds slower than our fastest previous ‘B’ team, we completed what Paul Freary later called, “an epic day”. 1 Belgrave H ‘A’ 1:49:18; 2 Wells City H 1:50:34; 3 Aldershot F&D AC 1:51:26; 4 Bedford & County AC 1:51:44; 5 Harrow AC 1:52:41; 6 Newham & Essex Beagles 1:52:47; … 10 Belgrave H ‘B’ 1:55:48; 16 Belgrave H ‘C’ 1:57:31; 87 teams started, 69 finished.
